claims.text: Machine-learning models using Holder means of elemental properties can improve prediction of melting temperatures in high-entropy alloys relative to conventional methods.
Machine-learning models using Holder means of elemental properties can improve prediction of other melting properties in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed model uses Holder means of group number, atomic radius, and electronegativity as elemental-property descriptors.
The proposed model also uses cohesive energy and density as structural-property descriptors.
Machine-learning models can efficiently predict shear modulus for disordered high-entropy alloys with good accuracy.
Machine-learning models can efficiently predict bulk modulus for disordered high-entropy alloys with good accuracy.
Machine-learning capability for predicting elastic moduli can be extended to prediction of melting temperature and other melting properties.
The proposed approach is intended to apply under room-temperature computational-modeling conditions.
The validity of the proposed approach is limited to unspecified high-entropy-alloy compositions and property ranges.
Performance will be evaluated against conventional prediction methods using mean absolute error and coefficient of determination.
